issues.detail: The Greek 'ενος αιματος' (of one blood) is translated as 'từ một dòng máu' (from one blood/lineage), but the Greek structure implies that every nation of men was made 'of one blood' (unity/commonality), not necessarily 'from' a single source. However, more critically, the Vietnamese translation omits the word 'ανθρωπων' (of men/humanity) which qualifies 'εθνος' (nation).

The Greek 'παν εθνος ανθρωπων' refers to 'every nation of men'. The Vietnamese 'mọi dân ngoại' (all Gentiles/foreigners) is a theological interpretation that is not present in the Greek text, which simply says 'every nation of men'.
